![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225232/assets/08ce939458d5c298805692df7d10bed2abdcf81ec874da3f61dbe15f59fc141a.png)

A biologist records the heights $y$ (in meters) of several oak trees at certain times $x$ (in years) after they were planted. The scatter plot for the data and the corresponding linear regression line are shown above.  

According to the regression model, what is the residual for the highlighted datapoint?
question.worked_solution:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

$$
\text{Residual}=\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated}
$$

 

The highlighted datapoint has coordinates $(6,6.5).$ So, our actual value is $y=6.5.$

On the other hand, the point on the regression line that corresponds to $x=6$ has the $y$-coordinate $5.5.$ So, our estimated value is $\overset{^}{y}=5.5.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14225232/assets/eedd1cadb2ba49fb95f9e18f9bef365942e53521e6894a270c9a1e1474f3ed71.png)

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Residual} & =\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated} \\  & =y-\overset{^}{y} \\  & =6.5-5.5 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residual is $1\,\text{m}.$
